message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Time zone | Standard offset (UTC) | Daylight‑saving offset (UTC) |
|-----------|-----------------------|------------------------------|
| Los Angeles (PST/PDT) | UTC – 8 | UTC – 7 |
| Berlin (CET/CEST) | UTC + 1 | UTC + 2 |

Because both regions shift their clocks by the same amount (one hour forward in spring, one hour back in autumn), the **time difference stays constant at 9 hours**:

* **Berlin is always 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles.**

### Quick reference

| Current local time in Los Angeles | Corresponding time in Berlin |
|----------------------------------|------------------------------|
| 08:00 AM PST (winter) | 05:00 PM CET |
| 08:00 AM PDT (summer) | 05:00 PM CEST |

(If you’re looking at a specific date, just add 9 hours to the LA time to get Berlin time.)

**Note:**  
During the brief overlap when one region has switched to daylight saving and the other hasn’t yet (or vice‑versa), the difference can temporarily be 8 or 10 hours. This only happens for a few days around the transition dates (mid‑March and early‑November). For all other days, it’s a steady 9‑hour gap.
